<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918160_theRebbe_102" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918160_theRebbe_102__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the theme of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan" as the reversal of sea to dry land is specifically emphasized on Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan, the time the maamar was said, based on the connection of the three months Nissan, Iyar, and Sivan to the Exodus, the Omer, and the Giving of the Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on the known great precision in the discourses of our Rabbis and Leaders, also regarding the relevance of the topics in the discourses to the time of their delivery,</t>
    <t s="1">it must be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that the above matter—that the drawing down of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan"</t>
    <t s="3">(which is on Erev Rosh Chodesh)</t>
    <t s="4">is like the concept of turning the sea into dry land—</t>
    <t s="5">is primarily emphasized on Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan,</t>
    <t s="6">the time of the delivery of the maamar.</t>
    <t s="7">And this will be understood based on what is explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="8">regarding the concept of the first three months</t>
    <t s="9">(Nissan, Iyar, and Sivan),</t>
    <t s="10">that the reason that specifically in these three months the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned</t>
    <t s="11">[the month of spring, for in it you left Egypt,</t>
    <t s="12">on the first of the second month in the second year of their leaving the land of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="13">in the third month of the going out of the children of Israel from the land of Egypt],</t>
    <t s="14">is,</t>
    <t s="15">that the purpose of the Exodus from Egypt</t>
    <t s="16">[the concept of the month of Nissan]</t>
    <t s="17">is the Giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="18">[the concept of the month of Sivan],</t>
    <t s="19">and the Counting of the Omer</t>
    <t s="20">[the concept of the month of Iyar]</t>
    <t s="21">is the intermediary through which one comes from the Exodus from Egypt to the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="22">And based on this, it must be said,</t>
    <t s="23">that what is explained in the maamar—that the concept of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan"</t>
    <t s="24">(tomorrow is the new moon)</t>
    <t s="25">is like the concept of turning the sea into dry land—</t>
    <t s="26">is,</t>
    <t s="27">that this maamar</t>
    <t s="28">was said on Shabbat, Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan,</t>
    <t s="29">and since the month of Sivan, as well as the month of Iyar, come in sequence after the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="30">therefore,</t>
    <t s="31">on Erev Rosh Chodesh of these months, it is emphasized that the concept of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan"</t>
    <t s="32">(tomorrow is the new moon)</t>
    <t s="33">is analogous to the concept of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds—the conclusion of the Exodus from Egypt.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section parallels the three concepts of Exodus, Counting the Omer, and Giving of the Torah with the three concepts of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan," "Yifaked Moshavecha," and "V’Nifakadta."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">D)</t>
    <t s="1">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that the three concepts in the aforementioned three months—the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="3">the Counting of the Omer, and the Giving of the Torah—are analogous to the three concepts of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan... and you will be missed, for your seat will be vacant."</t>
    <t s="4">The Exodus from Egypt, which comes about through a drawing down from Above—similar to the concept of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan,"</t>
    <t s="5">and as mentioned above, that the drawing down of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan" is like the concept of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds,</t>
    <t s="6">the conclusion of the Exodus from Egypt.</t>
    <t s="7">The Counting of the Omer,</t>
    <t s="8">the descent of the Nefesh HaElokis and its enclothing in the Nefesh HaBahamis in order to refine the attributes of the Nefesh HaBahamis—similar to the concept of "Yifaked Moshavecha" and "you shall go down very low" in order to refine clarifications.</t>
    <t s="9">And the revelation of the Giving of the Torah, which comes after the work of clarifications of the Counting of the Omer,</t>
    <t s="10">which is higher even than the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt and the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds</t>
    <t s="11">(which were before the work)</t>
    <t s="12">—similar to the concept of "V’Nifakadta" after "Yifaked Moshavecha," which is higher even than the revelation of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan" that preceded it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that on Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan the emphasis of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan" is on empowering the concept of "V’Nifakadta" (the segulah of descent), while on Erev Rosh Chodesh Iyar the emphasis is on empowering the concept of "Yifaked Moshavecha" (the work of clarifications).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, it may be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that on Erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan,</t>
    <t s="2">the emphasis of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan" is primarily regarding that through the drawing down of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan," the empowerment for the concept of "V’Nifakadta" is drawn,</t>
    <t s="3">the concept of segulta</t>
    <t s="4">(and segulah)</t>
    <t s="5">that is in "V’Shilasta."</t>
    <t s="6">And as explained in the maamar, the connection of "and you shall go down very low" to the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds</t>
    <t s="7">("Vayomer Lo Yehonasan"),</t>
    <t s="8">that the explanation of "and you shall go down very low... and you shall sit by the stone of Ezel" is that the concept of segulta</t>
    <t s="9">(segulah)</t>
    <t s="10">[which is drawn through the clarifications]</t>
    <t s="11">will be drawn downward</t>
    <t s="12">("you shall go down very low")</t>
    <t s="13">even into Asiyah</t>
    <t s="14">("the stone of Ezel"),</t>
    <t s="15">like the revelation of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds, which was drawn even into the lowest levels of Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="16">"a maidservant saw..."</t>
    <t s="17">And on Erev Rosh Chodesh Iyar,</t>
    <t s="18">the emphasis of "Vayomer Lo Yehonasan" is primarily that through this the empowerment for the concept of "Yifaked Moshavecha" is drawn,</t>
    <t s="19">the concept of segul that is in "V’Shilasta,"</t>
    <t s="20">the work of clarifications.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
